back_translation: Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem eleven years. His mother's name was Hamutal, daughter of Jeremiah, from Libnah.
Zedekiah did evil in the sight of the LORD, just as everything Jehoiakim had done.
Because of the anger of the LORD all this happened in Jerusalem and Judah, until he cast them out from his presence. And Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.

So in the ninth year of Zedekiah's reign, on the tenth day of the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and all his army marched against Jerusalem; they encamped around the city and built a siege wall all around it.
And the city was kept under siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.
By the ninth day of the fourth month the famine in the city was so severe that the people of the land had no food.

Then the wall of the city was breached, and though the Chaldeans were surrounding the city, all the soldiers fled out of the city by night by way of the gate between the two walls near the king's garden, and headed toward the Arabah.
But the army of the Chaldeans pursued the king and overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho, and all his army was scattered from him.
They seized the king and brought him up to the king of Babylon at Riblah in the land of Hamath, where he pronounced judgment on him.
At Riblah the king of Babylon slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes, and he also killed all the officials of Judah.
Then the king of Babylon put out Zedekiah's eyes, bound him with bronze shackles, and brought him to Babylon, keeping him in custody in prison until the day of his death.
On the tenth day of the fifth month, in the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard, a servant of the king of Babylon, entered Jerusalem.
He burned the house of the LORD, the royal palace, and all the houses of Jerusalem; every important building he burned with fire.
And the whole army of the Chaldeans under the captain of the guard broke down all the walls around Jerusalem.

Then Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard carried into exile some of the poorest people, the people who remained in the city, those who had deserted to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the craftsmen.
But Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard left behind some of the poorest of the land to tend the vineyards and till the fields.

As for the bronze pillars that were in the house of the LORD, together with the stands and the bronze Sea that were in the house of the LORD, the Chaldeans broke them up and carried all the bronze to Babylon.
They also took away the pots, shovels, wick trimmers, sprinkling bowls, dishes, and all the bronze articles used in the temple service.
The captain of the guard also took away the basins, censers, sprinkling bowls, pots, lampstands, dishes, and drink-offering bowls—everything made of pure gold and pure silver.

As for the two pillars, the one Sea, the twelve bronze bulls that were underneath, and the stands that King Solomon had made for the house of the LORD, the bronze of all these articles was beyond weighing.
Each pillar was eighteen cubits high and twelve cubits in circumference, four fingers thick, and hollow.

On top of it was a bronze capital; the height of one capital was five cubits, with a network and pomegranates all around the capital, all of bronze; and the second pillar had pomegranates and was the same.
On the sides there were ninety-six pomegranates; all the pomegranates around the network were a hundred.
The captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the second priest, and the three doorkeepers.

And from the city he took a court official who was in command of the men of war, and seven of the king's close advisers who were found in the city, and the scribe of the army commander who mustered the people of the land, and sixty men of the people of the land who were found in the city.
Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard took them and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.
At Riblah in the land of Hamath the king of Babylon struck them down and put them to death. So Judah was carried into exile from its own land.
These are the people Nebuchadnezzar carried into exile: in the seventh year, 3,023 Jews;
in the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar, 832 people from Jerusalem;
in the twenty-third year of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard carried away 745 Jews; in all, 4,600 people.

In the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah, on the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month, Evil-merodach king of Babylon, in the year he became king, showed favor to Jehoiachin king of Judah and brought him out of prison.
He spoke kindly to Jehoiachin and set his throne above the thrones of the other kings who were with him in Babylon.
So Jehoiachin changed out of his prison clothes, and he ate at the king's table regularly all the days of his life.
And the king of Babylon gave Jehoiachin a regular daily allowance all the days of his life, until the day of his death.
